decisions: Five total Windows attempts only for EPERM/EBUSY at exact rename or owned unlink operations; delays 25/50/100/200 ms. Never repeat registry transforms or delete destinations.
Before replacement validate parents, owned staging identity/contents and the final destination version/identity. Revalidate every retry; preserve cancellation and no-overwrite hard-link creation.
Only a dedicated FileWriteCleanupError class establishes a committed creation when stage cleanup fails. Registry retains commit state and separate lock cleanup failures with bounded sanitized fields.
Close acquired lock even if identity inspection fails; do not delete unknown/replaced/linked locks or stages. Preserve first staging write/sync error if close also fails.
One implementation owner and one read-only peer, standing owner authorization; no model-consuming execution.
limitations: Original 3ca uninstall EPERM, earlier4985 journal EPERM and prior failures remain unexplained; later successful tests do not identify their causes.
retained means owned cleanup was not confirmed; external interference may have moved or removed the pathname.
Committed means link/rename completion was observed; it is not proof of directory-fsync durability or unchanged state after return.
Pathname checks are not an atomic filesystem compare-and-swap or hostile-local-writer sandbox; cancellation cannot interrupt OS I/O.
Fault-injection tests use real temporary files and selected OS-branch substitutions; no actual native lock-conflict reproduction is claimed.
Full third-party/runtime/image/transitive rights, actual supported-client integrations, complete AUG/DCP/WEB acceptance remain open.
